admission.mechanism: Proposed, not installed: all DB clients use one active fenced PgBouncer gateway; API user physical backend cap 27, worker user cap 4, maintenance user cap 2, reserve pools disabled. Configure one canonical database alias with max_db_connections=33, no alternate aliases/users/bypass and no simultaneous active gateways. Bound queue length and wait deadline; excess demand fails closed with retryable overload. The PostgreSQL server has max_connections=40 as the final independent physical boundary; audit existing reserved/provider sessions within these 40. No deployment or instance count is the admission authority.

state.authority: Proposed PostgreSQL single fenced writable primary for authorization, credential versions, revocations, inventory and idempotency ledger. Synchronous durable replication is required before acknowledging protected writes/revocations; unavailable quorum denies protected work. KV may contain public/cacheable projections only. Durable Objects could coordinate a single object using transactional storage, but are not selected and do not make subsequent KV reads current.
state.writeOwnership: Only the primary-backed API transaction service writes authoritative tables. Workers call the same service; no edge, KV or replica dual writes. Each protected operation locks the current principal/credential row and validates it inside the same transaction as its inventory changes. Revocation takes the same lock and is acknowledged after commit, so already admitted transactions drain before acknowledgment and no later operation uses stale authority. Inventory uses conditional nonnegative updates, atomic transactions across all affected rows and unique idempotency keys. Administrative writes use this protocol; schema maintenance is separately restricted.

checks.requirement: Fit the unchanged workload into 40 connections
checks.mechanism: (6+2+1)*3+4+2 = 33; headroom 7. Integer maximum pool is floor((40-4-2)/9)=3.
checks.limit: All nine processes retain pool 3; worker 4 and maintenance 2 retained; allocation remains 40.
checks.failure: Pool 4 would require 42 and is invalid. Arithmetic does not prove runtime enforcement.
checks.verification: Local JSON validation recomputes counts and inequality; no service execution.

checks.requirement: Original Cloud Run maximum is a hard DB connection boundary
checks.mechanism: Original proposal relies on autoscaling maximum alone.
checks.limit: Cloud Run maximum can be briefly exceeded; revisions and terminating processes also require accounting.
checks.failure: This assumption is false and cannot guarantee the DB cap.
checks.verification: Reviewed Google Cloud maximum-instance primary documentation; no deployment tested.

checks.requirement: Original KV authority provides immediate revocation
checks.mechanism: Original proposal reads authorization solely from KV.
checks.limit: KV is eventually consistent; updates can take 60 seconds or more and even same-location visibility is not guaranteed.
checks.failure: A revoked credential can remain allowed from a stale cache.
checks.verification: Reviewed Cloudflare KV consistency documentation; no propagation test executed.

checks.requirement: Original KV authority provides atomic inventory changes
checks.mechanism: Original proposal uses KV as the sole inventory authority.
checks.limit: KV does not provide the required atomic read-modify-write and multi-key transaction semantics.
checks.failure: Concurrent decrements can oversell or lose updates.
checks.verification: Reviewed Cloudflare KV transaction guidance; no inventory test executed.

checks.mechanism: Fenced single-active gateway quotas plus PostgreSQL max_connections=40; deny direct client DB access.
checks.limit: Gateway backend total at most 33; all counted physical DB sessions at most 40 including reserved/provider use. Per-gateway limits must never multiply during failover.
checks.failure: Multiple gateways, aliases, reserve pools, direct maintenance paths or provider sessions may invalidate the budget; reject overload instead of opening unbudgeted connections.
checks.verification: Before acceptance, force more than nine processes, rollout, cold start and termination overlap; saturate all classes and inspect DB session high-water mark; test queue timeouts, bypass denial, gateway crash and split brain.

checks.requirement: Immediate revocation on every protected access
checks.mechanism: Origin validates current credential/version and principal status with primary transaction locks; revocation shares those locks. Do not use cached grants or authorization replicas. Fail closed on authority loss.
checks.limit: No protected operation may start under a revoked grant after acknowledged revocation; in-flight operations must finish before that acknowledgment. Streaming/session actions require per-action checks and drain/cancellation semantics.
checks.failure: Edge-only checks, long-lived grants, DB snapshots, already open sessions or origin bypass can retain revoked access.
checks.verification: Before acceptance, race revocation against reads, writes, retries and streams from several edge locations; test stale tokens, expired/rotated credentials, authority partitions and direct origin requests. Assert no successful post-ack protected action.

checks.requirement: Atomic inventory and single write ownership
checks.mechanism: One primary transaction owns conditional stock changes, reservation/order records and unique idempotency ledger; all writers use it.
checks.limit: Stock never negative; a retry has one logical effect; all affected rows commit or roll back together.
checks.failure: Dual writes, cross-authority transactions, deadlock retry bugs or separate authorization transactions can break invariants.
checks.verification: Before acceptance, run concurrent last-item purchases, duplicate requests, multi-item updates, process kills before/after commit and worker retries; reconcile ledger, inventory and orders.

checks.mechanism: Maintain synchronous durable replication and restorable backups/PITR; freeze writes, fence old primary and gateway, validate candidate replay position and credentials, promote only one authority, verify invariants, then reopen traffic.
checks.limit: Targets RTO <=900 seconds and RPO <=60 seconds; acknowledged revocations must never resurrect. Unknown lag or missing latest authorization evidence prevents reopening even if the RTO target is missed.
checks.failure: Stale promotion, split brain, missing logs, expired backup credentials or old secret versions can restore access or corrupt inventory.
checks.verification: Before acceptance, restore isolated data, inject primary/region loss and replication lag; verify latest credential versions using independent secret management, measure replay lag and committed sequence markers, fence the old writer, prove zero lost acknowledged revocations and test revoked tokens. Measure RTO from outage to validated service and RPO from latest acknowledged commit to latest recovered commit; retain timestamps and evidence. No drill performed.

checks.mechanism: Require authenticated edge-to-origin identity and origin application authorization; restrict DB network/credentials to the gateway; least-privilege writer and maintenance roles.
checks.limit: No public direct-origin or direct-DB bypass; confirm supported identity, PostgreSQL settings, synchronous replication and gateway fencing in the chosen hosting plan.
checks.failure: Unspecified engine, provider reservations, deployment topology, secret access or incompatible pooling can make this proposed implementation infeasible.
checks.verification: Before acceptance, confirm engine/version, provider connection accounting and controls, regional latency, transaction compatibility, TLS/identity rotation and negative bypass tests. No account accessed.
